q: Why are several elevators often grouped around a common lobby in larger buildings?
o: To consolidate passenger waiting, wayfinding and group control
To eliminate the need for hoistways
ref: Standard elevator engineering terminology and conventional traction/hydraulic elevator components.
n: Grouping supports clear circulation and allows coordinated dispatching of multiple cars.

q: Which elevator is typically designed with dimensions and load characteristics suitable for transporting a patient on a bed or stretcher?
ref: Standard elevator engineering terminology and conventional traction/hydraulic elevator components.
n: Hospital/bed elevators are planned to accommodate beds/stretchers, attendants, and associated circulation requirements.

q: Two elevator groups serve the same lobby, but one is dedicated to floors 2–10 and the other to floors 11–20. This is:
ref: Standard elevator engineering terminology and conventional traction/hydraulic elevator components.
n: Assigning separate floor ranges to separate groups is elevator zoning.

q: Which design change usually increases potential handling capacity, all else being equal?
o: Increasing the number or capacity of appropriately sized cars
Reducing every car to the smallest possible size
ref: Standard elevator engineering terminology and conventional traction/hydraulic elevator components.
n: More suitable car capacity and/or additional cars can increase the number of passengers moved, though actual performance depends on speed, stops, loading, zoning, and control strategy.

o: A group of elevators arranged to serve related traffic and usually a common lobby
A financial office beside a lift
ref: Standard elevator engineering terminology and conventional traction/hydraulic elevator components.
n: An elevator bank groups multiple cars so passenger demand can be served collectively and dispatched efficiently.

q: A dumbwaiter is primarily intended for:
o: Transporting small goods rather than passengers
ref: Standard elevator engineering terminology and conventional traction/hydraulic elevator components.
n: A dumbwaiter is a small service lift intended for materials such as food, documents, or small goods, not passenger transport.

q: A 20-storey building has severe morning up-peak traffic. Which planning concept is most directly relevant to reducing unnecessary stops by assigning different floor ranges to different groups?
ref: Standard elevator engineering terminology and conventional traction/hydraulic elevator components.
n: Zoning is used in taller buildings to divide service ranges and improve traffic performance.

q: In elevator traffic analysis, 'interval' most nearly refers to:
o: Average time between successive car departures/arrivals serving the main terminal under the selected traffic condition
Time required to paint the car
ref: Standard elevator engineering terminology and conventional traction/hydraulic elevator components.
n: Interval is a key measure of the frequency with which elevator service is available at the main terminal.

q: Elevators are most directly examined in architecture as part of:
ref: PRC Board of Architecture, Architecture Licensure Examination Syllabi — Utilities Systems coverage.
n: Elevators are building utility/vertical transportation systems and fit the utilities systems portion of architectural technical knowledge.

q: Which elevator system raises the car primarily by hydraulic pressure acting on a cylinder/plunger or equivalent hydraulic arrangement?
ref: Standard elevator engineering terminology and conventional traction/hydraulic elevator components.
n: Hydraulic elevators use pressurized fluid to move a piston/plunger or roped-hydraulic arrangement.

q: A high-rise system in which one group serves lower floors and another serves upper floors is an example of:
ref: Standard elevator engineering terminology and conventional traction/hydraulic elevator components.
n: Lower- and upper-floor elevator groups are a classic zoning strategy.

q: In elevator planning, 'handling capacity' generally refers to:
o: The amount of passenger traffic a system can transport within a stated period under defined assumptions
The structural capacity of the roof only
The amount of air in the lobby
ref: Standard elevator engineering terminology and conventional traction/hydraulic elevator components.
n: Handling capacity is a traffic-performance concept, commonly expressed as people or a percentage of building population transported over a defined interval.

q: What does 'MRL' mean in elevator terminology?
ref: Standard elevator engineering terminology and conventional traction/hydraulic elevator components.
n: MRL means machine-room-less: major drive/control equipment is arranged without a conventional separate elevator machine room, subject to manufacturer and code requirements.

q: Which elevator type normally uses ropes or belts passing over a drive sheave, with the car balanced by a counterweight?
ref: Standard elevator engineering terminology and conventional traction/hydraulic elevator components.
n: Traction elevators use a drive sheave and suspension means, typically with a counterweight, to move the car.

o: Using one elevator for all buildings in a city
Assigning different elevator groups to different ranges of floors
ref: Standard elevator engineering terminology and conventional traction/hydraulic elevator components.
n: Zoning divides building floors among elevator groups to reduce unnecessary stops and improve high-rise traffic performance.
